title: Adaptive Noise Cancellation Using the Least Mean Squares Algorithm: Implementation and Parameter Analysis
content: Unwanted broadband noise is a major challenge in many communication and measurement systems. This report focuses on the design, MATLAB implementation, and performance analysis of Adaptive Noise Cancellation (ANC) system using the Least Mean Squares (LMS) algorithm. The system works by using a reference signal that is related to the unwanted noise but independent of the original desired signal. An FIR adaptive filter updates its coefficients continuously using the LMS algorithm to estimate the noise and remove it from the corrupted input signal. In this study, the desired signal is a 50 Hz sine wave sampled at 1 kHz for two seconds and mixed with Gaussian noise having a standard deviation of 0.6. A correlated reference noise signal is created by passing the same noise through a first-order moving average filter. The system performance is evaluated through time-domain signal recovery, mean squared error (MSE) learning curves, FFT-based spectral analysis, and parameter testing for different step sizes (μ) and filter orders (M). Using the baseline parameters of M = 16 and μ = 0.005, the system improves the input SNR from 1.20 dB to 9.32 dB, giving an 8.13 dB improvement. The best performance is achieved with M = 4 while keeping μ fixed, resulting in an output SNR of 11.06 dB, which corresponds to an improvement of about 9.86 dB. The findings agree with adaptive filter theory: smaller step sizes provide slower but more stable convergence, larger step sizes can make the system unstable, and excessively large filter orders may reduce performance due to higher misadjustment. Finally, the report discusses possible future improvements, including Filtered-x LMS methods and real-time embedded implementations for practical acoustic ANC applications.
